headline: Beijing AI bar haemorrhaging cash offering unlimited free DeepSeek coding tokens with $1.50 drink
summary: The AGI Bar in Beijing gives away roughly 10 times more free AI tokens than drinks sold, with its owner admitting the venture is "completely losing money."
details: The AGI Bar in Beijing's Zhongguancun tech hub offers unlimited free DeepSeek AI tokens with its signature 9.9 yuan ($1.50) drink. Owner Song De, an independent AI developer, admits the bar is "completely losing money."
The bar reportedly gives away 10 times more AI tokens than drinks sold. It runs AI inference locally on two Nvidia DGX Spark mini-PCs, which are displayed prominently.
Each Nvidia DGX Spark unit, costing around $4,699, pairs a 20-core Arm CPU with a Blackwell GPU and 128GB of unified LPDDR5X. A matched pair costs approximately $9,400.

The AI agent available via the bar's WiFi is a distilled or aggressively quantized version of DeepSeek's models. DeepSeek's full V3 and V4 models range from 671 billion to 1.6 trillion parameters, exceeding the local hardware's 256GB pooled memory.

DeepSeek recently suspended a fundraising round targeting a $71 billion valuation after its founder reportedly discussed the company's reliance on Nvidia chips. He also estimated China lags leading U.S. labs by 12 to 18 months in AI compute.

These admissions highlight Beijing's struggle to reduce its AI sector's dependence on American silicon. DeepSeek was previously urged to train its R2 model on Huawei's Ascend hardware before reverting to Nvidia GPUs due to repeated failures.

The AGI Bar in Beijing's Zhongguancun tech hub offers unlimited free DeepSeek AI tokens with its signature 9.9 yuan ($1.50) drink. Owner Song De, an independent AI developer, admits the bar is "completely losing money."

Each Nvidia DGX Spark unit, costing around $4,699, pairs a 20-core Arm CPU with a Blackwell GPU and 128GB of unified LPDDR5X. A matched pair costs approximately $9,400.

The AI agent available via the bar's WiFi is a distilled or aggressively quantized version of DeepSeek's models. DeepSeek's full V3 and V4 models range from 671 billion to 1.6 trillion parameters, exceeding the local hardware's 256GB pooled memory.

DeepSeek recently suspended a fundraising round targeting a $71 billion valuation after its founder reportedly discussed the company's reliance on Nvidia chips. He also estimated China lags leading U.S. labs by 12 to 18 months in AI compute.

These admissions highlight Beijing's struggle to reduce its AI sector's dependence on American silicon. DeepSeek was previously urged to train its R2 model on Huawei's Ascend hardware before reverting to Nvidia GPUs due to repeated failures.
